35046c96facf:
• « The Mother of God and the “Burning Bush” » – icon painted on glass, modelled on several depictions, one of them being the first icon (on this theme) to reach our country (in the 1940s), at the venerable foundation of Saint Antim the Iberian, the Antim Monastery in Bucharest. Many generations of the Church's servants and of the faithful have prayed before this icon, and it also inspired the well-known hesychast movement “The Burning Bush”, a group that kept the fire of faith alive in the hearts of many Romanians, especially during the communist rule.
• According to the painters' manual, the icon “The Burning Bush” shows a large eight-pointed star in the form of overlapping rhombuses, with the Mother of God holding the Saviour in her arms at their centre. Four of the eight points are red, representing the fire, and the other four, coloured green, symbolise that the bush did not burn but remained whole. On the points of the red star are the symbols of the four Holy Evangelists: the angel (Saint Matthew), the lion (Saint Mark), the ox (Saint Luke) and the eagle (Saint John), and on the four points of the green star the Holy Angels are depicted.
• If you would like a similar icon, contact me and we will settle the details. This icon is not available; it was made to order.
82e7e48b92ce:
On 20 July the Romanian Orthodox Church celebrates the ascent into heaven of the Holy Great Prophet Elijah the Tishbite, a saint honoured as a great wonderworker and bringer of rain in times of drought

Depicted in icons either at the mouth of his cave (which can still be visited today, in the land of Choziba) with the ravens sent to feed him, or in the chariot of fire in which he was taken up to heaven, or in both (as in the icon shown today), the Holy Great Prophet Elijah the Tishbite is the Old Testament figure dearest and most familiar to the Christian conscience everywhere

We welcome the great feast with an icon on glass made after the icon «The Ascent of the Holy Prophet Elijah into Heaven, with scenes from his life» (Șcheii Brașovului, early 19th century), in the collection of the Leon Sculy Logothetti family of Iași

Happy name day to all who celebrate!🌺

936a327e7ab4:
❈ 14 September | The Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross

✧ Răzvan Codrescu: “By its vertical, the cross signifies the bond between heaven and earth, the aspiration to higher things, the uprightness of a life illumined by faith. Its horizontal signifies the all-embracing embrace of the world through sacrificial love, the calling and gathering of all around the holy axis that leads to Heaven. The point where they cross, where the horizontal and the vertical “commune”, signifies the essential centre of our existence, our right place in the mystery of salvation, which is possible through man's co-working in grace with God, through the joining of matter to spirit and of the created spirit (the human soul) to the uncreated Spirit (the Holy Spirit).”

✧ The icon (model: Nicula, mid-19th century) that we are showing you in honour of the great feast was given to a holy place of worship built in memory of the martyrs of the Romanian communist prisons
796f14485b03:
> The theme of this icon (model: workshop in Șcheii Brașovului, last decades of the 19th century) is the scene of the Coronation of the Mother of God. The scene shows the Holy Trinity (the spiritual unity of the three divine persons): Jesus Christ carrying the Cross of the crucifixion, God the Father with the orb and sceptre (the insignia of the Almighty), and the Holy Spirit (as a white dove framed by the sun) sending down His blessing. The first two hold a crown above the head of the Virgin Mary (kneeling, dressed in a white maphorion, with her hands crossed on her chest). The figures are ”held up” by clouds. 🤍

8d0285eba92b:
(†) "The Ascension of the Lord" is the Feast of the Day, and today's icon on glass (model: Nicula, early 19th century) shows this theme.
  (†)   Christ has ascended!
 "Forty days after the Resurrection of Christ and ten days before the Descent of the Holy Spirit, we celebrate the bodily Ascension into heaven of the incarnate Son of God. The Ascension of Christ shows what man's destination is: the human nature He took on was fully transfigured; it was not dissolved in its union with the divine nature. If it becomes invisible after the Ascension, this is due to its deification. Indeed, man's purpose is not to lose himself in the world, for then the most important factor of reality would be lost.
 The bodily Ascension into heaven is a testimony that man was created for eternity, for the Son presents Himself to the Father as God and also as Man.
 Through His Ascension, Christ not only shows where man must arrive, but becomes the way and the power for man to reach that state. He sits on the divine throne of glory, yet He also dwells in the hearts of those who love Him. This is how we can understand the paradox: Christ is ascended, and yet on the way to ascension with each one of us..." (crestinortodox.ro)
